```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(car)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))

# Cleaned data provided for Case 31 (Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav)
aware_lab <- c("Unaware", "Aware but Have Not Used", "Aware and Have Used")

case31 <- read_sav("Case31_Data_efcu_4.sav") |>
  zap_labels() |>
  mutate(q13r = factor(q13_r, levels = 1:3, labels = aware_lab))

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
```

# Data and Measures

-   **Data:** `Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav` (cleaned data provided for the case), *N* = `r nrow(case31)` members.
-   **Recoded variables used:** q13r (1 = Unaware, 2 = Aware but Have Not Used, 3 = Aware and Have Used) and q8r (1 = Very Low to 5 = Very High; "No opinion" set to missing).

# H1: Awareness of Regular Share Accounts and Adequacy of Financial Services

> **H1:** Members' awareness of the regular share accounts will influence their opinions on the adequacy of financial services in meeting members' needs.

-   **Constructs and roles:** awareness of the regular share account (IV); adequacy of financial services in meeting members' needs (DV)
-   **Operationalization:** q13r (ordinal, 3 groups); q33 (interval, 1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree)
-   **Statistics:** descriptive statistics, followed by a one-way ANOVA. A one-way ANOVA fits because the IV has three groups and the DV is interval; a *t*-test can compare only two groups.

## Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h1-desc
#| tbl-cap: "Adequacy of financial services (q33) by awareness of the regular share account (q13r)"

h1_desc <- case31 |>
  group_by(Awareness = q13r) |>
  summarise(n = n(), Mean = round(mean(q33), 2), SD = round(sd(q33), 2),
            Min = min(q33), Max = max(q33)) |>
  bind_rows(case31 |>
              summarise(Awareness = "Overall", n = n(), Mean = round(mean(q33), 2),
                        SD = round(sd(q33), 2), Min = min(q33), Max = max(q33)))
kable(h1_desc)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-h1-means
#| fig-cap: "Mean adequacy of financial services (q33) by awareness of the regular share account"

h1_desc |>
  filter(Awareness != "Overall") |>
  mutate(Awareness = factor(Awareness, levels = aware_lab)) |>
  ggplot(aes(Mean, Awareness)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a78d6", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Mean)), hjust = -0.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 5), breaks = 1:5) +
  labs(x = "Mean of q33 (1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree)",
       y = "Awareness of regular share account")
```

## One-way ANOVA

-   $H_0$: all group means are equal ($\mu_{Unaware} = \mu_{Aware, not used} = \mu_{Aware, used}$)
-   $H_A$: at least one pair of group means is different

### Normality of Residuals

```{r}
#| label: h1-normality

h1_aov <- aov(q33 ~ q13r, data = case31)
h1_shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals(h1_aov))
h1_shapiro
```

### Homogeneity of Variance

```{r}
#| label: h1-levene

h1_levene <- leveneTest(q33 ~ q13r, data = case31)
h1_levene
```

### ANOVA Test

```{r}
#| label: h1-anova

h1_sum <- summary(h1_aov)
h1_sum
```

Because the residuals are not normally distributed, the Kruskal-Wallis test (the non-parametric alternative) is run as a check.

```{r}
#| label: h1-kruskal

h1_kw <- kruskal.test(q33 ~ q13r, data = case31)
h1_kw
```

### Post-hoc Analysis

```{r}
#| label: h1-tukey

# After a significant ANOVA
h1_tukey <- TukeyHSD(h1_aov)
h1_tukey
```

```{r}
#| label: h1-wilcox

# After a significant Kruskal-Wallis test: pairwise Wilcoxon tests, Bonferroni-adjusted
h1_wilcox <- pairwise.wilcox.test(case31$q33, case31$q13r, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni",
                                  exact = FALSE)
h1_wilcox
```

## Insights about H1

```{r}
#| label: h1-inline

h1_F  <- h1_sum[[1]][["F value"]][1]
h1_df <- h1_sum[[1]][["Df"]]
h1_p  <- h1_sum[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
tk    <- h1_tukey$q13r
m     <- setNames(h1_desc$Mean[1:3], aware_lab)
```

::: callout-note
## Insights about H1

-   Awareness of the regular share account is related to how well members think the CU's financial services meet their needs, supporting H1 (*F*(`r h1_df[1]`, `r h1_df[2]`) = `r round(h1_F, 2)`, *p* = `r fmt_p(h1_p)`; Kruskal-Wallis *p* = `r fmt_p(h1_kw$p.value)`) (@tbl-h1-desc, @fig-h1-means).
-   The relationship is negative. Members who are aware of the account **and have used it** rate the adequacy of services lowest (*M* = `r m[3]`), below both members who are unaware (*M* = `r m[1]`, Tukey *p* = `r fmt_p(tk[2, "p adj"])`) and members who are aware but have not used it (*M* = `r m[2]`, Tukey *p* = `r fmt_p(tk[3, "p adj"])`). The two lower awareness groups do not differ (Tukey *p* = `r fmt_p(tk[1, "p adj"])`). The pairwise Wilcoxon tests show the same pattern.
-   Members who have actually used the regular share account are the least satisfied with how well the CU meets their needs.
:::

# H2: Opinion on CU Loan Rates vs. Belief that CU Rates Are Lower

> **H2:** Members will not be different in their opinion on CU's loan rate (q8r) and the degree to which they agree that CU's loan rate is lower than competitors (q30).

-   **Operationalization:** q8r, opinion about the rates charged on funds borrowed (interval, 1 = Very Low to 5 = Very High); q30, CU loan rates are lower than others (interval, 1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree)
-   **Statistics:** descriptive statistics, followed by a paired-samples *t*-test. A paired test fits because the same members answered both questions, so the two scores are not independent samples.

## Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h2-desc
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive statistics for q8r and q30 (members who answered both)"

h2 <- case31 |>
  select(q8r = Q8_r, q30) |>
  drop_na()

h2 |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "y") |>
  group_by(Variable) |>
  summarise(n = n(), Mean = round(mean(y), 2), SD = round(sd(y), 2),
            Min = min(y), Max = max(y)) |>
  mutate(Variable = c("q8r: Opinion about rates charged on funds borrowed",
                      "q30: CU loan rates lower than others")) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-h2-freq
#| fig-cap: "Response distributions for q8r and q30 (members who answered both)"

h2 |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "y") |>
  mutate(Variable = dplyr::recode(Variable,
                           q8r = "q8r: Loan rates (1 = Very Low, 5 = Very High)",
                           q30 = "q30: CU rates lower (1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree)")) |>
  count(Variable, y) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(y), n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a78d6", width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~Variable, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Response", y = "# of members")
```

## Paired-Samples t-test

-   $H_0: \mu_{q8r} = \mu_{q30}$ (mean difference = 0)
-   $H_A: \mu_{q8r} \neq \mu_{q30}$

```{r}
#| label: h2-ttest

h2_t <- t.test(h2$q8r, h2$q30, paired = TRUE)
h2_t
```

## Insights about H2

::: callout-note
## Insights about H2

-   Members' opinion on the CU's loan rate (*M* = `r round(mean(h2$q8r), 2)`) and their agreement that the CU's loan rate is lower than competitors' (*M* = `r round(mean(h2$q30), 2)`) are not different (*t*(`r h2_t$parameter`) = `r round(h2_t$statistic, 2)`, *p* = `r fmt_p(h2_t$p.value)`), supporting H2 (@tbl-h2-desc).
-   Both scores sit near the middle of their scales (@fig-h2-freq): the most common answers are that the CU's loan rates are "Average" (`r round(mean(h2$q8r == 3) * 100, 1)`%) and "Uncertain" whether they are lower than competitors' (`r round(mean(h2$q30 == 3) * 100, 1)`%).
-   Members do not see the CU's loan rates as an advantage, which may help explain why they borrow elsewhere.
:::
